strike_b.why_the_facing_gate_missed_it: THE MIRROR TEST IS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO A FRONT-TURN. scripts/check-facing.mjs compares IoU(anchor,clip) vs IoU(anchor,mirror(clip)). A frontal pose is roughly left-right symmetric, so as-is and mirrored score nearly the SAME and BOTH score low against a side-profile anchor — it reads as weak agreement, not as a defect. Measured here: f33 as-is 0.226 vs mirrored 0.180, f49 0.220 vs 0.169. as-is still won at every frame, so a literal mirror-test read returns PASS on a clip that is square to camera for half its length.
strike_b.new_gate: qa-boss/check-frontturn.mjs written in response. Signals: selfSym = IoU(silhouette, its own mirror) after bbox-normalising (side profile asymmetric = LOW, square to camera = HIGH) and aspect = bbox w/h. Within ir48s own kit it separates cleanly — idle sym 0.288 aspect 0.63 run 0/97 · strike_a v2 sym 0.486 aspect 0.74 run 9/97 · strike_b v1 sym 0.526 aspect 1.32 run 48/97. THE HARD TELL IS ASPECT CROSSING 1.0: a silhouette wider than it is tall cannot be a side profile. NOTE the tool is explicitly NOT calibrated to convict across the roster (it flags 77 of 97 shipped clips at default thresholds, mostly ko clips that correctly END COLLAPSED and characters whose anchors are already wide) — see the calibration box in the script.

ko_suffix_rule: build-prompt.mjs enforces it: `ko` is the ONE off-anchor state, so the shared suffix's weapon lock ('keeps ... in his hands the whole time and never drops or swaps them') and anchor lock ('begins and ends on the EXACT same reference stance') are STRIPPED for ko only. Pasting them verbatim gives the model two mutually exclusive orders — his ko body says the fan and sword SLIP FROM HIS HANDS and he ENDS COLLAPSED. lady-kurotachi.md carries this as a hand-written operator note; ir48's prompt file does NOT, so the rule now lives in the builder instead of depending on whoever fires remembering it.
